rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil defines major sins as sins ending in Hell, and indecencies as sins carrying a prescribed worldly penalty.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: كبائر الإثم، يعني: كل ذنب ختم بالنار، والفواحش يعني: كل ذنب فيه الحد

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi recite the phrase in the singular, kabīr al-ithm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (كبير الإثم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular faʿīl, like faʿūl, can convey abundance; the author supports this with Qur'anic examples and poetry.
rows.anchor: وفعيل قد جاء يعني به الكثرة كما أن فعولا كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular form is suitable because the genitive verbal noun means sins generally, not one particular sin, so the singular conveys a plural sense.
rows.anchor: ليس يراد به إثم بعينه، إنما يراد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singular and plural forms can both express the intended abundance, as the Qur'an alternates between singular and plural for enemy.
rows.anchor: فأفرد، وجمع في قوله: {ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who read the plural kabāʾir do so because the meaning is plural, while ithm itself can be singular in form and abundant in sense.
rows.anchor: وأما من جمع فقال: {كبائر الإثم} فلأنه في المعنى جمع

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation takes al-lamam as minor sins, namely acts falling short of fornication.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: إلا ما كان دون الزنا

rows.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: An unintended glance is lamam; repeating the glance makes it a sin rather than lamam.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي عنه: اللمم النظرة عن غير تعمد، فإن أعاد النظر فليس بلمم وهو ذنب

rows.speaker: نافع بن جبير بن مطعم
rows.claim: Al-lamam means what falls short of sexual intercourse.
rows.anchor: وعن نافع بن جبير بن مطعم: هو ما دون الوقاع

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، وأبو هريرة، ومسروق، والشعبي، وطاووس
rows.claim: These authorities likewise define lamam as what is short of fornication.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن مسعود، وأبي هريرة، ومسروق، والشعبي، وطاووس، قالوا: ما دون الزنا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet describes a person's destined share of fornication through looking, speech, kissing, touching, walking, and desire, while the genitals either confirm or deny it.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا بما روى أبو هريرة أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "إن الله -عز وجل- كتب على ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If intercourse occurs, the person has committed fornication; without it, the lesser acts remain lamam.
rows.anchor: فإن تقدم فرجه كان زان وإلا فهو اللمم

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والضحاك، ومقاتل
rows.claim: They define lamam as sin between the limits of a worldly penalty and a punishment threatened in the afterlife; prayers expiate it for those who avoid major sins.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الزبير، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والضحاك، ومقاتل: هو ما بين الحدين، حد الدنيا

rows.speaker: العوفي والحكم عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas gives the same view: lamam is a sin with neither a worldly penalty nor a promised afterlife punishment, forgiven for those who avoid major sins.
rows.anchor: وهي رواية العوفي، والحكم عن ابن عباس، وهؤلاء قالوا: اللمم تكفره الصلوات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second main interpretation is a person falling into a sin once, then repenting and not returning to it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إلا اللمم} قال: يلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that if God forgives, He forgives abundantly, since no servant is free of error.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- يقول: "إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan defines lamam as a person committing an act once and then desisting.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الرجل يلم المرة ثم ينزع

rows.speaker: السدي عن أبي صالح
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports Abu Salih's definition: a person falls into a sin but does not repeat it; Ibn Abbas praised this answer, and the view is also attributed to Mujahid.
rows.anchor: وروى السدي عن أبي صالح، قال: سألني رجل عن اللمم، فقلت: هو الرجل يلم بالذنب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When told Abu Salih's definition, Ibn Abbas said that a noble angel had helped him reach it.
rows.anchor: فحدثت بذلك ابن عباس قال: لقد أعانك عليها ملك كريم

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains alamma bi-kadhā as approaching something without entering into it, or taking only a little without persisting, since one has not gained control of it.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: يقال: ألم فلان بكذا إذا قاربه ولم يخالطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the minor-sins reading, lamam is approaching a major sin through a glance, kiss, or touch; on the repentance reading, it is a single lapse into fornication or drinking followed by repentance.
rows.anchor: فعلى ما ذكر اللمم ما قارب به من الكبيرة كالنظر والقبلة واللمس

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's line uses limām for an occasional visit, illustrating the sense of infrequency.
rows.anchor: قال جرير: بنفسي من تجنبه عزيز ... علي ومن زيارته لمام

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses limām as visits occurring now and then, without regularity or a fixed time.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه الأحيان على غير مواظبة ولا وقت معلوم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says Arabic uses ilām for nearness and approach, including the sense of almost doing something.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: والعرب تستعمل الإلمام في المقاربة والدنو، يقال: ألم بفعل كذا

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd says the phrase lamām of a month or two means approximately that period.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد: كان ذلك منذ شهرين أو لمامهما، ومنذ شهر أو لممه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: In the Prophetic saying about spring vegetation, Abu Ubayda explains aw yalimm as something that comes close to causing harm.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه أو يقرب إليه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying uses yalimm for what nearly causes an animal to die from overgrazing spring growth.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "وإن مما ينبت الربيع ما يقتل حبطا أو يلم

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd calls a tree that is nearly bearing fruit al-mulim.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: في أرض بني فلان من الشجر الملم كذا وكذا، وهو الذي قارب أن يحمل

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says a man described as dead or mulimm is near death, a palm is near bearing, and a lamma of hair nearly reaches the ear.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: فلان ميت أو ملم، أي قد قارب الموت، ونخل ملم قد قارب الإطعام

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: The cited verse about Zayd illustrates a person close to death, while lamma describes hair that has nearly reached the ear.
rows.anchor: وزيد ميت كمد الحبارى ... إذا بانت لطيفة أو ملم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative alimmū means grant us the smallest share of your visit, as the following verse illustrates.
rows.anchor: وقوله: ألمم، معناه اجعل لنا من زيارتك أدنى حظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under both main interpretations, the exception is external rather than an exception of an item belonging to the preceding category.
rows.anchor: وأما الاستثناء في قوله: {إلا اللمم} على القولين جميعا استثناء خارج

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says lamam was not permitted and is not itself a major sin or indecency; the phrase means unless someone happens to lapse into such an act, under the first interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: لم يؤذن لهم في اللمم وليس اللمم من الفواحش ولا من كبائر الإثم

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad likewise denies that lamam is permitted; he reads the exception as meaning that if they lapse, they repent, comparing it with seeking God's face in 92:19–20.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: لم يبحهم اللمم، ومعناه استثناء ليس من الأول

rows.speaker: ابن أحمر
rows.claim: Ibn Ahmar's licentious verse pretends that God permitted lamam to deceive a woman; the source says he knew it was not permitted, as her righteous response shows.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر-وأراد أن يخدع من يخاطبه- فقال

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say lamam belongs to the same category as indecencies: a person commits the indecency once, then repents and stops, which the word itself implies.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: اللمم على القول الثاني من جنس الفواحش والاستثناء وقع من الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the external-exception reading, because treating lamam as an exception from the same category would make it seem permitted.
rows.anchor: والصحيح هو الأول؛ لأن هذا يؤدي إلى إباحة اللمم

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت، وزيد بن أسلم، وابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view says lamam means sins committed before Islam; it arose after polytheists reproached Muslims for having once acted as they had.
rows.anchor: زيد بن ثابت، وزيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Amr defines lamam as anything short of associating partners with God; on this reading, major sins and indecencies lead to shirk.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني: هو قول عبد الله بن عمرو قال: اللمم ما دون الشرك

rows.speaker: الناس
rows.claim: The general tendency is to follow the first two interpretations, minor sins or a lapse followed by repentance.
rows.anchor: والناس على القولين الأولين

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers the repentance interpretation: a person approaches a sin without persisting, since ilām in Arabic means doing something briefly rather than remaining at it.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو إسحاق الثاني منهما، قال: اللمم هو أن يكون الإنسان قد ألم بالمعصية ولم يصر

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq argues from Arabic usage that ilām means approaching something briefly without continuing in it.
rows.anchor: والإلمام في اللغة يوجب أنك تأتي الشيء في الوقت ولا تقيم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's vast forgiveness as applying to one who committed such a lapse and repented.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لمن فعل ذلك وتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajnna is the plural of janīn, a child in the womb; the name derives from being concealed, as does the word for someone buried under earth.
rows.anchor: أجنة جمع جنين، وهو الولد ما دام في البطن، سمي جنينا لأنه مستور

rows.speaker: عمرو
rows.claim: Amr's verse uses janīn for a person buried in a grave.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو: ولا شمطاء لم يترك شقاها ... لها من تسعة إلا جنينا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: God knows what every soul will do, what it will make, and what its end will be.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: علم الله من كل نفس ما هي عاملة وما هي صانعة وإلى ما هي صائرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ glosses God's knowledge as encompassing first and last.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو أعلم أولا وآخرا

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: They report that people boasted, saying they had prayed, fasted, and done good deeds, after which the verse forbade self-purification.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي، ومقاتل: كان ناس يقولون: صلينا وصمنا وفعلنا وفعلنا، فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes the command as forbidding people to boast that they have done particular deeds.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: لا يقولن أحدكم عملت كذا وفعلت كذا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others interpret the command as forbidding people to declare themselves innocent or praise themselves; Zaynab bint Abi Salama's naming prompted the Prophetic correction.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معناه لا تبرؤوها ولا تمدحوها، يدل على هذا ما روى أن زينب بنت أبي سلمة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When Zaynab bint Abi Salama was called Barrah, the Prophet said not to declare yourselves pure, since God knows your piety better, and renamed her Zaynab.
rows.anchor: قال النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "لا تزكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to praise oneself for qualities one does not possess; taken generally, it encourages humility and worship while avoiding ostentation and self-admiration.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: لا تزكوها بما ليس فيها. ويجوز أن يكون المعنى على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God knows best who is righteous and obedient.
rows.anchor: أي بر وأطاع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains piety here as sincerity in one's deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: أخلص العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference is to what was in Abraham's scriptures.
rows.anchor: {وإبراهيم} يعني: وفي صحف إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawfiyah means completion and fulfillment; the author illustrates it with God fully paying people's wages.
rows.anchor: معنى التوفية في اللغة الإتمام والإكمال، يقال: وفيته أجره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء والكلبي
rows.claim: One view says Abraham fulfilled by delivering to his people what God had commanded him.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء والكلبي: بلغ ما أمر به قومه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil gives the same interpretation: Abraham delivered God's command to his people.
rows.anchor: بلغ ما أمر به قومه، وهو قول مقاتل

rows.speaker: الفراء وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ and Ibn Qutayba choose the interpretation that Abraham delivered God's command to his people.
rows.anchor: بلغ ما أمر به قومه، وهو قول مقاتل، واختيار الفراء، وابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، وإبراهيم، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية، وعكرمة
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, and Ikrima also say Abraham conveyed the words from God to his people.
rows.anchor: وهو قول سعيد بن جبير، وإبراهيم، ومجاهد، وأبي العالية، وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the first interpretation, the particle an in the following verse is accusative as governed by waffā.
rows.anchor: وأن على هذا القول في محل النصب بقوله: (وفي)

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled every duty God imposed, including sacrificing his son, enduring the fire, passing the tests of 2:124, circumcision, and pilgrimage rites.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى: (وفي) أكمل ما يجب لله تعالى عليه بالطاعة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers the view that Abraham completed all obligations through obedience and patience.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي إسحاق، وعلى هذا موضع أن في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second view, an may be genitive as an appositive to what was in the scriptures, meaning that no soul bears another's sin.
rows.anchor: خفض على البدل من قوله: {بما في صحف}

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Alternatively, an may be nominative with an omitted pronoun, as if asking what the scriptures contain and answering that no burden-bearer bears another's burden.
rows.anchor: وقال: يجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع على إضمار هو

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The verse means that no man is held responsible for another person's sin.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة عن ابن عباس: لا يؤخذ الرجل بذنب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the offer to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira that someone could give him payment and carry his sins; no one is punished for another's crime.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا إبطال لقول من قال للوليد بن المغيرة: أعطني شيئا وأحمل عنك ذنوبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports that exegetes say from Noah until Abraham, a person was taken for the sins of a brother or son, until Abraham conveyed this teaching; it applies in both worldly life and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: كان من لدن نوح إلى زمان إبراهيم يؤخذ الرجل بذنب أخيه وابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also taught that one who calls people to error bears a burden like the burdens of those who follow, as stated in 16:25.
rows.anchor: وذكره رسولنا محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أن من دعا إلى ضلالة كان عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In thumma yujzāhu, the pronoun refers to the person's effort; the verb can mean repaying someone for his work or effort.
rows.anchor: أي يجرى الإنسان سعيه، والضمير للسعي يقال: جزيت فلانا عمله وسعيه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poem uses jazā for recompensing someone's effort, as evidence for the verb's sense.
rows.anchor: إن أز علقمة بن سعد سعيه ... لا أجزه ببلاء يوم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jazāʾ al-awfā means the most complete and perfect recompense; Abu Ishaq glosses it as fully rewarding the deed.
rows.anchor: و {الجزاء الأوفى} الأكمل والأتم، قال أبو إسحاق: أي يجزى عمله أوفى جزاء

rows.speaker: المتقدمون من المفسرين
rows.claim: Earlier commentators interpret the phrase as death in worldly life followed by resurrection to life.
rows.anchor: المتقدمون من المفسرين حملوا هذا

rows.speaker: المتأخرون من المفسرين
rows.claim: Later commentators also say God caused fathers to die and brought sons to life, like the wording in 45:24.
rows.anchor: والمتأخرون منهم ذكروا وجوها أخرى، منها: أنه أمات الآباء، وأحيا الأبناء

rows.speaker: المتأخرون من المفسرين
rows.claim: Other later interpretations say God caused the sperm to die and brought the living being to life, or made an unbeliever dead through disbelief and a believer alive through faith, paralleling 30:19 and 6:122.
rows.anchor: ومنها أنه أمات النطفة وأحيا النسمة، وأمات الكافر بالكفر وأحيا المؤمن بالإيمان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes the pronoun in We left it as a sign to refer to Noah's ark, and says God left it on al-Judi until the earliest members of this community saw it.
rows.anchor: وهو قول قتادة، قال: أبقى الله سفينة نوح على الجودي حتى أدركتها أوائل هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says the sign is the event and the affair of Noah's ship, left as a lesson; 69:11–12 supports this by describing the ship as a reminder.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: المعنى تركنا هذه الفعلة وأمر سفينة نوح آية، أي علامة ليعتبر بها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses the question as asking whether anyone will remember that the warning is true, learn from it, and fear.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: فهل من متذكر يعلم أن ذلك حق فيعتبر ويخاف

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The underlying form is mudh-takir; tāʾ changes to dāl and dhāl assimilates into dāl, since the voiced dāl better matches the voiced sound than the voiceless tāʾ; compare muzdajir.
rows.anchor: وأصله مذتكر، ولكن التاء أبدل منها الدال، والذال من موضع التاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي عن سيبويه
rows.claim: Abu Ali cites Sibawayh for a form with dhāl in al-dhikr, supported by a verse of Ibn Muqbil.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: وقالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The high frequency of the dāl forms ادكر and مدكر made the root resemble patterns such as taqwā, taqiya, and taqāt.
rows.anchor: لما كثر تصرف الكلمة بالدال نحو ادكر، وهل من مدكر أشبهت تقوى وتقية وتقاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question how was My punishment and warnings magnifies the punishment and makes the listeners marvel at it.
rows.anchor: كيف استفهام عن تلك الحالية، ومعناه التعظيم لذلك العذاب. والتعجب منه للسامعين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats nudhur as a verbal noun meaning My warning.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: النذر هاهنا مصدر معناه: فكيف كان إنذاري

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says nudhur and nadhīr are verbal nouns like munkar and nakīr, and points to the usage in 77:6.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي: النذر والنذير مثل المنكر والنكير وهي جميعا مصدران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks how Noah's warning was when his people rejected his call to faith, and it warns the polytheists.
rows.anchor: المعنى: كيف كان إنذاري إياهم، إذ دعاهم نوح إلى الإيمان فلم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: One interpretation takes dhikr as memorization and recitation; the Qur'an is the only revealed book people recite entirely from memory.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن المراد بالذكر هاهنا الحفظ والقراءة، وهو قول سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says that without God's making the Qur'an easy, no one could speak God's words; God made it accessible to creation.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لولا أن الله يسر القرآن ما استطاع أحد أن يتكلم بكلام الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj observes that followers of other religions generally read the Torah and Gospel from a text and rarely memorize them entirely as Muslims memorize the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: قيل: إن كتب أهل الأديان نحو التوراة والإنجيل إنما يتلوها أهلها نظرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the recitation reading, the question urges people to recite, study, learn, and understand the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول معنى قوله {فهل من مدكر} أي هل من ذاكر يذكره، وقارئ يقرأه

rows.speaker: مطر الوراق
rows.claim: Matar al-Warraq paraphrases the question as asking whether there is a seeker of knowledge who will be helped.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مطر الوراق: هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes dhikr to mean reflection and taking heed of what the Qur'an contains.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني: أن معنى الذكر هاهنا الاعتبار والتفكر، قال مقاتل: يعني ليتذكروا ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Qur'an easy by giving it clear, understandable rather than difficult wording and by setting out admonitions and warnings, as in 26:195.
rows.anchor: هوناه بأن جعلنا ألفاظه سهلة مفهومة لا صعبة متعقدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reflection reading, the question asks whether anyone will take admonition, reflect, and fear.
rows.anchor: أي من متعظ معتبر خائف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God made the Qur'an easy for anyone willing to take admonition.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، قال: يريد سهلنا القرآن لكل متعظ

rows.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reading says God made each thing in a form suited to it, such as woman to man, she-ass to donkey, mare to horse, and gender-appropriate clothing.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي عن ابن عباس: إنا كل شيء جعلنا له شكلا يوافقه ويصلح له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God assigned each created thing its proper measure, as in 65:3; al-Rabiʿ agrees.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: قدر الله لكل شيء من خلقه قدره الذي ينبغي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets the verse as God having decreed punishment for the criminals, linking it to what precedes.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني أنه قدر لهم العذاب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says 54:45–49 was revealed concerning the Qadariyya after Quraysh's polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن # قوله: {إن المجرمين}

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi also says the passage was revealed to rebuke the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: نزلت تعييرا لأهل القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Qadariyya interpretation, the criminals are the polytheist deniers of predestination and their counterparts in this community, who share their status.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول المراد بالمجرمين القدرية المشركون وإخوانهم من قدرية هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet recited these verses and said they were revealed concerning people in the later community who deny God's decree.
rows.anchor: أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قرأ هذه الآيات وقال

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports that a delegation from Najran asked whether deeds were theirs while lifespans belonged to God; after asking why they would be punished for written sins, the Prophet called them God's disputants on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي ذر قال: قدم وقد نجران على النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- فقالوا: الأعمال إلينا

rows.speaker: النبي عن عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: The Prophet said a herald will summon God's disputants on Judgment Day, meaning the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: ويؤكد هذا ما روى عمر بن الخطاب -رضي الله عنه- عن رسول -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the Torah states that the Qadariyya will be dragged face-down in the Fire.
rows.anchor: ويزيد وضوحا هذه الجملة ما روي عن كعب أنه قال: نجد في التوراة أن القدرية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
rows.claim: Ata attributes to Ibn Abbas the report that the verses were revealed about polytheist Qadariyya who argued with the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وهو قول عطاء عن ابن عباس أن الآيات نزلت في القدرية من المشركين الذين جادلوا رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: On the predestination reading, everything created is measured and written in the Preserved Tablet before it occurs, supported by 54:52.
rows.anchor: يدل على هذا قوله: {وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر} ذكر ذلك أبو إسحاق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created all beings according to decree and created good and evil for them; the best good is felicity and the worst evil is wretchedness.
rows.anchor: وروى الوالبي عن ابن عباس قال: خلق الله الخلق كلهم بقدر، وخلق لهم الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlayhā refers to the earth mentioned earlier at 55:10; every creature that moves across the earth will perish.
rows.anchor: أي على الأرض، وقد سبق ذكرها في قوله {والأرض وضعها}

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: They report that the angels concluded the people of earth had perished when this verse was revealed, then became certain of their own destruction when 28:88 was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: لما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة: هلك أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says a reader should not pause after the statement that all on earth perish, but continue into the statement that the Lord's face remains.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} فلا تسكت حتى تقول: {ويبقى وجه ربك

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the Face to mean the Lord's manifestation through His signs, just as a human face makes the person apparent.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن المعنى ويبقى ربك الظاهر بأدلته كظهور الإنسان بوجهه

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes Face as a term for something eminent, so the phrase means the Lord, the exalted Master.
rows.anchor: الثاني: ويبقى ربك وهو السيد المعظم، والوجه يذكر بمعنى الشيء المعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhū is an adjective of wajh; if wajh were merely an adjunct of rabbika, the adjective would be dhī rather than nominative dhū.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الوجه هاهنا صلة لقوله (ذو) بالرفع وهو من صفة الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jalāl denotes God's greatness and majesty and His right to praised attributes for His beneficence and favor; the word derives from jalla, to be great.
rows.anchor: والجلال عظمة الله وكبرياؤه واستحقاقه صفات المدح بإحسانه وإنعامه

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says jalāl is used only of God.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي: ولا يقال الجلال إلا لله تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali cites poetry in which jalāl describes someone other than God, while allowing that the poem may be pre-Islamic and that al-Asmaʿi meant only God deserves the term after Islam.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: قد جاء الجلال في غير الله سبحانه وأنشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikram can mean God's honoring His prophets through grace, or servants honoring God through worship and praise for His favors.
rows.anchor: وللإكرام هاهنا معنيان. أحدهما: إكرام الله تعالى أنبياءه فهو مكرمهم بلطفه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Hasan and al-Kalbi take ikram as God's honoring the people of His religion and loyalty and His generosity in forgiving His creatures.
rows.anchor: والأول معنى قول الحسن: الذي يكرم أهل دينه وولايته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes ikram as meaning that none is more honorable, majestic, or great than God.
rows.anchor: والثاني معنى قول ابن عباس: الذي لا أكرم منه ولا أجل ولا أعظم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the two gardens as lower in rank than the first pair.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أدنى من الأوليين

rows.speaker: ابن جريج ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil describe four gardens: the first pair for the foremost and the latter pair for the people of the right and their followers; the latter gardens are inferior, as most commentators hold.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: هي أربع: جنتان للمقربين السابقين كما وصفنا وجنتان لأصحاب اليمين والتابعين

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators, including Ibn Zayd and al-Kalbi, hold that the second pair is lower in merit than the first pair.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أكثر المفسرين أن هاتين دون الأوليين في الفضل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the opposite view: the first two gardens are gold and silver, while the latter two are ruby and emerald and therefore superior.
rows.anchor: وذهب الضحاك إلى ضد ما ذكر هؤلاء فقال: الجنتان الأوليان من ذهب وفضة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: On al-Kisaʾi's reading of this view, dūnahumā means in front of or before them; the author points back to the discussion at 2:23.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا قوله: {ومن دونهما} أي ومن أمامهما وقبلهما وهو قول الكسائي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says the gardens are so green that lushness makes them appear black.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: من خضرتهما قد اسودتا من الري

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says any green plant at the height of its greenness and freshness tends toward black.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وكل نبت اخضر، فتمام خضرته وريه أن يضرب إلى السواد

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Dahmah means blackness; al-Layth says a crop has idhāmm when its lushness has made it dark.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: ادهام الزرع إذا علاه السواد ريا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the gardens as intensely green, tending toward black.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: شديد الخضرة إلى السواد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi likewise describes them as green with blackness from the intensity of their greenery and lushness; intense green tends toward black.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: خضراوان قد علاهما سواد من شدة الخضرة والري

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says Arabs call green black; al-Qutami's verse describes the dark of night as green.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: الخضرة عند العرب سواد، وأنشد القطامي

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma also calls the shadow green in a line about an owl.
rows.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: في ظل أخضر يدعو هامة البوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression May God destroy their khadrāʾ means their blackness or abundance, using green as black.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا يقال أباد الله خضراءهم أي سوادهم

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma describes rain-covered vegetation as Abyssinian because its greenness has grown intense.
rows.anchor: فهو قول ذي الرمة أنشده ابن قتيبة في تفسير هذه الآية يصف غيثا:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following cited line describes a garden with intense greenness, calling it ḥawāʾ.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله أيضا أنشد أبو علي في تفسير هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali notes the reverse usage: drought is described as white; Aws's line says barren years gleam because they have no fertility or vegetation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: وعلى ضد هذا وصف الجدب البياض فقيل سنة شهداء
